newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to resow up to 500,000 ha of winter wheat.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to resow up to 500,000 ha of winter wheat.

text.p: Ukraine must resow up to 500,000 hectares of frost-damaged winter wheat during its spring sowing campaign, a senior agriculture ministry official said on Monday.
"We forecast that we will need to resow between 400,000 and 500,000 hectares," Valentyn Tymoshenko, deputy head of the ministry's crop department, told Reuters.
Tymoshenko said bouts of low temperatures this winter had affected fields without sufficient snow cover, especially in northern parts of the country.
Winter wheat grows best when covered with thick snow to protect it from potentially damaging frosts.
Tymoshenko said farmers, who planted 7.44 million hectares to winter wheat late last year out of a total 8.24 million hectares sown to winter grain, would resow damaged fields with spring crops.
Volodymyr Krut, deputy chairman of the Agriculture Sciences Academy, said the volume of resowing was "normal".
"Winter crops in most bread-producing parts of Ukraine are growing in good and satisfactory condition," he told Reuters.
Farmers resowed about 550,000 hectares from a total 5.67 million hectares last year, compared to nearly 800,000 hectares resown from 5.05 million hectares in 1995.
Krut added that most fields had enough moisture to create good spring growing conditions.

The scientist also complained about a shortage of fertilisers and pesticides, which could spoil government hopes for a better grain harvest this year compared to the 1996 harvest of 25.4 million tonnes -- one of the worst on record.
Agriculture Ministry officials have said the government planned to increase the 1997 grain harvest to 38 million tonnes. The 1995 grain harvest stood at 36.5 million tonnes.
Mykhaylo Zubets, deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture, has said Ukraine wanted to export three million tonnes of mostly winter wheat from last year's crop.
Earlier this month the government boosted domestic grain buying to 5.88 million tonnes from the 1997 crop after state orders totalled 5.0 million tonnes from the latest crop.
